reports.title: Roberto Bottello: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: CNWL failed in its duty of candour in relation to provision of evidence
SPA call handlers were not sufficiently trained in how to identify patients by using computer searches and by not seeking information appropriately
police officers may need reminding to use the phonetic alphabet and using the word for the month in a person's date of birth

psychiatric liaison nurses and psychiatric liaison doctors should have regard to and specifically consider diagnoses made by other doctors for example those who see such patients repeatedly in A&E as in this case
most section 136 usage is out of hours when there is less resource to respond from psychiatric services
use of film over glass in areas where patients are at increased risk of smashing windows should be more widespread in the NHSE estate
concerns.hazard: inadequate window safety in high‑risk areas

reports.title: Mia Gauci-Lamport: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: Lack of appropriate monitoring of Mia during the night
concerns.hazard: inadequate night monitoring of child with seizures
inadequate medical care documentation and oversight
failure of senior management to enforce robust care plan and governance

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures to fulfil the duty of candour obligation. The earlier case concerns mental health service evidence provision, while the later case concerns pediatric care governance and training.
links.earlier_quote: That CNWL failed in its duty of candour in relation to provision of evidence in this case.
links.later_quote: delay in fulfilling the Duty of Candour' obligations, ongoing staff training, ensuring robust procedures were in place alongside regular audits of clinical practice.
